accomplishments.text: Launched the Mission Control dashboard with a nightly scheduled sync that moves daily updates from the form queue to GitHub, summarizes them onto member pages, and now also logs each update to the club-wide technical log Google Sheet.
Settled the starter board's power design: USB-C carries data only (DFU and log download), and the 1S LiPo powers all logic.

Replaced 3 out-of-stock parts during design: IMU LSM6DSO32 → LSM6DSV32X (same ±32 g range and package, new register map), 10 µF capacitor 0805 → 0603, 100 kΩ resistor 0603 → 0402; moved the parts list from PDF to Markdown.
Removed GPS from v1 of the starter board and updated the lessons and parts list to match.
Published the Starter Flight Computer parts list and Lessons 1–3 for the new-member practice board.

data.focus: Scoping the primary flight computer's chip selection and pyro approach while extending the Mission Control dashboard. On Nov 19 he looked up metrics for evaluating candidate flight computer chips and went over BPS.space pyro setups with Max and Peter. On Nov 18 he added a step so dashboard daily updates are pushed automatically into Aydan's club-wide technical log Google Sheet, with the next step being to confirm it runs on the nightly schedule. The same day he discussed airbrakes sensing with Peter, Caleb and Dean Dezel, focusing on which sensors are needed for realistic simulations.

data.focus: Selecting parts for the avionics sensor suite and preparing its KiCad schematic. On Nov 19 he worked through the competition rule specifications for the scoring-data sensors and researched candidate barometers. Next he will finalize the barometer, pick a magnetometer, lay out the sensor-suite pin assignments and start the KiCad schematic.

data.focus: Starting the pyrotechnic system design for the FAR-OUT rocket after finishing key sections of the L1 STM32 board schematic. On Nov 19 he began researching pyro system approaches and went over BPS.space pyro setups with Alex, and plans to study recovery videos over the break. On Nov 17 he completed the board's 10-pin 1.27 mm SWD header (Samtec FTSH-105-01) and a buzzer circuit driving a CSS-J4B20 through an AO3400A N-MOSFET with a 10k gate pull-down and 1N4148W flyback diode; pyro circuits and footprint updates are next on that board.
